== Psychological profile ==
=== Personality === 
<!--Examples following this point focus on a general character study of Davros-->
[[File:The tiny pressure of my thumb.jpg|thumb|{{AltFloat}}|Davros contemplates holding the power of life and death in his hand. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Genesis of the Daleks (TV story)}})]]
Davros was malevolent and sadistic, and it was his ability to command and delegate that was most forceful and cold. Davros believed different species could not peacefully co-exist, so thought the utter extermination of all other races was the only way the Daleks could succeed at bringing peace. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Genesis of the Daleks (TV story)}}) Brilliant and driven, Davros relentlessly experimented to find the final form of the Kaled people. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Davros (audio story)}}) However, by creating the Daleks, he paradoxically believed that he had saved his own kind despite him not considering the Daleks to be Kaleds, ([[TV]]: {{cs|Genesis of the Daleks (TV story)}}) thinking that comparing the Daleks to the Kaleds was like saying a pearl was the heir to the stone that formed it. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Father of the Daleks (short story)}}) The Movellans' analysis of Davros noted that he prioritised his own survival above all else. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|The Triumph of Davros (audio story)}})

<!--Examples following this point focus on Davros's youth and early life-->
While he was of sound mind in his youth, Davros was already cold and indifferent to those around him at a young age, even to his own family, though he held a soft spot for his mother, [[Calcula (Innocence)|Lady Calcula]], from whom he inherited a lot of his fanaticism and ruthlessness. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Innocence (audio story)}}, {{cs|Corruption (audio story)}}, {{cs|Guilt (audio story)}}) However, he had no qualms about experimenting on the corpses of his mother and sister, ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Purity (audio story)}}, {{cs|Corruption (audio story)}}) and was perfectly willing to betray others simply to build and secure his own political position. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Davros (audio story)}})

[[File:Have pity!.jpg|thumb|{{AltFloat}}|Davros is betrayed by the Daleks. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Genesis of the Daleks (TV story)}})]]
Encouraged by his mother, Davros grew increasingly obsessed with his scientific experiments and personal ambitions. Already a feared and power-obsessed individual, ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Innocence (audio story)}}, {{cs|Purity (audio story)}}, {{cs|Corruption (audio story)}}, {{cs|Guilt (audio story)}}) the incident that crippled him and his overall experiences in the Thal-Kaled war left Davros a depraved and insane megalomaniac. He became tyrannical and more ruthless than before, tolerating no opposition to his will and dismissing fairness and democracy as "the creeds of cowards". However, when the Daleks turned on him, he begged them to show pity on him and his loyal scientists, only attempting to destroy them when they refused to obey him. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Genesis of the Daleks (TV story)}})

<!--Examples following this point focus on Davros' persona after his first resurrection-->
[[File:Davros reviews his troops.jpg|thumb|{{AltFloat}}|Davros takes command of the Daleks. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Destiny of the Daleks (TV story)}})]]
Following his reawakening from the extermination attempt, Davros instantly tried to ally himself with Daleks, ([[TV]]: {{cs|Destiny of the Daleks (TV story)}}) though he was still bitter on how easily they betrayed and used him. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Resurrection of the Daleks (TV story)}}) This led him to making the Imperial Daleks. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Revelation of the Daleks (TV story)}}) 

<!--Examples following this point focus on Davros' persona as the Emperor of the Daleks-->
Following his failure to use the Hand of Omega, Davros developed a completely Dalek personality that identified itself as "the Emperor". The Emperor was highly critical of Davros, berating him for being a fool and allowing himself to be defeated so many times by both the Doctor and the Daleks. After the Davros personality was seemingly destroyed, the Emperor seized full control, ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Terror Firma (audio story)}}) though later accounts attain that Davros was able to reclaim his identity. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Stolen Earth (TV story)}})

<!--Examples following this point focus on Davros' persona after the Last Great Time War-->
[[File:DavrosJE3.jpg|thumb|{{AltFloat}}|Davros declares the end of the [[omniverse]]. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Journey's End (TV story)}})]]
After his rescue from the Time War, Davros remained as narcissistic as ever, referring to the reality bomb as "the apotheosis of [his] genius", ([[TV]]: {{cs|Journey's End (TV story)}}) but he also showed a dislike of pride and vanity, admonishing the [[Supreme Dalek (The Stolen Earth)|Dalek Supreme]] for displaying pride and distastefully noting the "arrogance" in the [[Tenth Doctor]]'s voice. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Stolen Earth (TV story)}}) He also seemed to have been driven more insane than before, having been consumed by a desire to completely destroy all of creation under [[Dalek Caan]]'s manipulations. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Journey's End (TV story)}})

<!--Examples following this point focus on Davros' thoughts on and relationship with the Daleks-->
[[File:A single simple Dalek succeeded.jpg|thumb|{{AltFloat}}|Davros praises [[Dalek Caan]]. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Stolen Earth (TV story)}})]]
While Davros had made the Daleks into a race that could only hate, he himself had always tried to get them to love him as their father. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Third Wise Man (short story)}}) However, he also maintained that, if the Daleks were to return the love he had for them, they would no longer be his children. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Father of the Daleks (short story)}}) When challenged by the [[Fourth Doctor]], Davros refused to accept the idea that the Daleks were evil, instead believing they would bring peace by becoming the sole life-forms of the universe. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Genesis of the Daleks (TV story)}}) Even years later, he maintained to the [[Twelfth Doctor]] that the Daleks existed "for the ultimate good of the universe". ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Magician's Apprentice (TV story)}})

During the lead up to the [[Last Great Time War]], Davros felt the pride of a father when the Daleks told him they had declared war on the Time Lords. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Father of the Daleks (short story)}}) Davros had joy in his voice when he saved the Daleks from the [[Nightmare Child]], yet the Daleks would never care about his sacrifice. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|The Third Wise Man (short story)}}) He had many moments of parental pride and fondness for the Daleks, being eager to talk about, and learn of, their accomplishments ([[TV]]: {{cs|Destiny of the Daleks (TV story)}}, {{cs|The Magician's Apprentice (TV story)}}) yet paradoxically thought little of their intelligence and abilities, believing that they could not progress without him. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|The Triumph of Davros (audio story)}})

For all his desire to rule the Daleks before and throughout the [[Imperial-Renegade Dalek Civil War]], ([[TV]]: {{cs|Revelation of the Daleks (TV story)}}) he eventually accepted arrangements that kept him alive and involved in their affairs. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Journey's End (TV story)}}) He claimed the Daleks had a genetic fault that made them respect him and showcase mercy towards him. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Witch's Familiar (TV story)}}) Instead of ruling over them, he wanted his "children" to love him as their father and sought to simply to be involved in their empire. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Father of the Daleks (short story)}}) 

<!--Examples following this point focus on Davros' thoughts on and relationship with the Doctor-->
[[File:The Doctor and Davros catch up.jpg|thumb|{{AltFloat}}|Davros talks with the [[Sixth Doctor]]. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Revelation of the Daleks (TV story)}})]]
Although he respected the [[Fourth Doctor]] as a fellow scientist, he refused to give in to his request to make the Daleks into less vicious creatures. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Genesis of the Daleks (TV story)}}) He also told the [[Sixth Doctor]] that he was the closest thing he had left to a friend, reflecting that "in some strange dream of history" they may have actually been friends. Even though the Doctor insisted that the two of them were not friends, Davros nonetheless noted they were both scientists who had "been through a lot" together. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Davros (audio story)}}) Over the years, Davros and the Doctor had several truces where they met with each other on [[Christmas]]. During one meeting on the [[Red Moon of Xhe]], Davros found himself enjoying their Christmas truce, but he claimed it was only because of the low oxygen affecting him. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Father of the Daleks (short story)}}) Davros once joked that the Doctor "slaughter[ing]" Daleks and him "slaughter[ing]" Time Lords was the "conventional means of communication" in their dynamic. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Witch's Familiar (TV story)}})

[[File:Why do you hesitate?.jpg|thumb|{{AltFloat}}|Davros talks with the [[Twelfth Doctor]]. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Witch's Familiar (TV story)}})]]
During the [[war in the Medusa Cascade]], though he proclaimed the Doctor to be arrogant ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Stolen Earth (TV story)}}) and took a sadistic pleasure in reminding the Doctor of how many people had died for him, Davros still sought a moment to catch up with him "after so very long". ([[TV]]: {{cs|Journey's End (TV story)}}) During his scheme to trick the Twelfth Doctor into giving his regeneration energy, Davros stated that he had always admired the Doctor and claimed to wish that they, at least once, could be on the same side. While it later appeared that Davros had been putting on an act, he also displayed joy when the Doctor told him Gallifrey had been saved, as it meant the Doctor had saved his own kind, as opposed to Davros' attempt to save the Kaleds. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Witch's Familiar (TV story)}}) Even after he betrayed him, Davros believed he and the Doctor could have created "[[The Hybrid|a true hybrid]]" if they had worked together. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Secrets of the Dalek Laboratory (feature)}})

<!--Examples following this point focus on Davros' benevolence-->
<!--Examples following this point focus on Davros' miscellaneous traits-->
[[File:Davros and the Doctor laugh.jpg|thumb|{{AltFloat}}|Despite his ill health, Davros manages to laugh at his own joke. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Witch's Familiar (TV story)}})]]
Davros did possess a sense of humour, however rarely it was expressed, such as when he coldly quipped that informing the beneficiaries of his Necros-produced protein that they would be eating their own relatives would have created "consumer resistance". ([[TV]]: {{cs|Revelation of the Daleks (TV story)}}) When the Doctor admitted his doubt that Davros was honestly dying despite seeing his failing health, Davros humorously told him that he was "not a good [[doctor]]", at which both men laughed at in a moment of union. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Witch's Familiar (TV story)}})

== Appearance ==
[[File:The Eye of the Creator.jpg|thumb|{{AltFloat}}|The painting ''[[The Eye of the Creator]]'' ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Dalek: The Astounding Untold History of the Greatest Enemies of the Universe (short story)}})]]
As a child, Davros had the skin tone similar to a Caucasian human, brown hair and two functioning blue eyes. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Magician's Apprentice (TV story)}}) However, his body was mangled by a [[Davros's accident|Thal bombardment]]. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Davros (audio story)}}, {{cs|Corruption (audio story)}}) By the [[Movellan]]s' definition, Davros became a [[humanoid]] [[mutant]] ([[TV]]: {{cs|Destiny of the Daleks (TV story)}}) after he had taken on a cyborg form and [[Davros's chair|life-support system]].

[[File:Davros uprooted from his chair.jpg|thumb|{{AltFloat}}|The extent of Davros's bodily damage. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Witch's Familiar (TV story)}})]]
His skin was discoloured and his body crippled by the bombardment, leaving him without the use his legs or his left arm. His Kaled body was humanoid, though a [[Davros's eye|blue lens]] in his forehead replaced his lost vision, allowing him a semblance of sight. He had only [[Davros's right hand|his right hand]], which he used to operate controls on his chariot that could perform functions for controlling doors, the [[Mark III travel machine]]s, or his own life support system. He had a helmet-like arrangement of wires and plastic tubes suspended over his head, ([[TV]]: {{cs|Genesis of the Daleks (TV story)}}) and was rendered more machine than man, with his lungs, heart, speech, hearing and sight being mechanically or electronically aided. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Doctor Who and the Destiny of the Daleks (novelisation)}})

[[File:Davros returns in Resurrection of the Daleks.jpg|thumb|{{AltFloat}}|Davros is released from cryogenic imprisonment. ([[TV]]: {{cs| Resurrection of the Daleks (TV story)}})]]
As Davros's life-support system maintained the function of his vital organs and revivified necrotising tissue, his appearance underwent subtle changes over time. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Dalek Combat Training Manual (reference book)}}) Following his cryogenic imprisonment, Davros's face gained a yellowish, sagging appearance, ([[TV]]: {{cs|Resurrection of the Daleks (TV story)}}) while, after the Time War, a darker colour had returned to his face. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Stolen Earth (TV story)}}) During a meeting the [[Eighth Doctor]], Davros claimed that he had been "clinging" onto his physical form but regretted the decision, deciding that he did not need his withered body to remain himself. ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|Terror Firma (audio story)}}) However, Davros always made sure his repairs kept him with a similar image whenever he needed to be "reconstructed". Upon meeting the [[Eleventh Doctor]], he questioned why he did so instead of changing himself into a younger form. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Father of the Daleks (short story)}})

After [[Bostock]] fired a gun which destroyed most of his right hand, ([[TV]]: {{cs|Revelation of the Daleks (TV story)}}) Davros had his hand replaced with a claw ([[COMIC]]: {{cs|Emperor of the Daleks! (comic story)}}) or a prosthetic substitute ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|The Juggernauts (audio story)}}) which eventually came to be a metallic replica of his lost appendage. [[TV]]: {{cs|The Stolen Earth (TV story)}}) He was capable of projecting [[electricity|electric]] shocks from both his mechanical hand, ([[TV]]: {{cs|Journey's End (TV story)}}) as well as his eye. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Journey's End (TV story)}})

[[File:Davros opens his eyes.jpg|thumb|{{AltFloat}}|Davros opens his eyes. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Witch's Familiar (TV story)}})]]
While tricking the [[Twelfth Doctor]] into using his regeneration energy to rejuvenate his dying body, it was revealed that while Davros could still open and use his real eyes, but it required him to shut down the artificial eye in the middle of his forehead. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Witch's Familiar (TV story)}})

=== Chair designs ===
[[File:Davros electrocutes Orcini.jpg|{{AltFloat}}|thumb|Davros uses [[Davros's chair|his chair]] to hover. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Revelation of the Daleks (TV story)}})]]
Davros was originally seen by the [[Fourth Doctor]] sitting upright in a [[Davros's chair|life-support chariot]] resembling the base of a Dalek. Davros's blue eye appendage mirrored the look of a Dalek's eyestalk lens. A metal brace was attached to his head, and wires were plugged into his skull. Davros also had a throat microphone implant to enhance his damaged voice. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Genesis of the Daleks (TV story)}}) By the [[Necros Incident]], Davros's chair had anti-gravity gravitors that enabled him to hover. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Revelation of the Daleks (TV story)}})

[[File:Prepare the assault shuttle.jpg|thumb|{{AltFloat}}|Davros's Emperor casing. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Remembrance of the Daleks (TV story)}})]]
By the time that Davros had risen to become the [[Dalek Emperor|Emperor]] of the [[Imperial Dalek]] faction during the [[Imperial-Renegade Dalek Civil War]], his life-support chariot no longer featured a button with which he could deactivate his life support, ([[AUDIO]]: {{cs|The Curse of Davros (audio story)}}) as it had when he had first met the Doctor on Skaro. ([[TV]]: {{cs|Genesis of the Daleks (TV story)}}) During the [[Imperial-Renegade Dalek Civil War]], Davros sat in a bloated dome. His head was cradled by metal braces from which wires trailed down into the hidden body of the Dalek shell. His eyes were hollow scars and the skin of his cheeks was withered and cracked. ([[PROSE]]: {{cs|Remembrance of the Daleks (novelisation)}})

Davros later dispensed with his skull wires and throat microphone. However, he retained his head brace. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Stolen Earth (TV story)}}) His artificial eye was evidently connected to his nervous system and susceptible to pain, as he visibly winced after [[Missy]] jabbed him in the mechanical eye. ([[TV]]: {{cs|The Witch's Familiar (TV story)}})

== Behind the scenes ==
=== Purpose ===
[[Terry Nation]] saw Davros as a voice for the Daleks. In [[DWM 250|DWM #250]], he commented:
{{quote|The Daleks, when they have to make any kind of long speech, are immensely boring creatures. You can't have a Dalek doing four or five sentences in a row, so I wanted someone to speak for them. The thing that was half-man and half-Dalek was a perfect example of this, and I made sure he was not killed... he actually became a very good plot piece.|[[Terry Nation]]|DWM 250}}

=== Anatomical controversy ===
In {{cs|Remembrance of the Daleks (TV story)}}, only Davros's head was seen inside the [[Dalek Emperor|Imperial]] [[Casing]], poking out of a tangle of wire. As [[Ben Aaronovitch]] revealed in [[DWM 147]], his intention was that Davros's head was all that was left of his body, having decided to upgrade himself into a Dalek to protect his life after being threatened at gunpoint by the Doctor in {{cs|Resurrection of the Daleks (TV story)}}. Aaronovitch suspected that he had even only kept his face so that he could use it "to sneer at the Doctor" during what he thought would be their final meeting, and was planning to have it removed also in the long run. This intent is alluded to in the story when the [[Seventh Doctor]] notes that Davros had "discarded the last vestiges of a human form".

However, in the filmed episode, the visible movements of [[Terry Molloy]]'s shoulders underneath the mass of wires obscured Aaronovitch's intent, which would been followed inconsistently in later stories. The comic story {{cs|Emperor of the Daleks! (comic story)}}, a prequel to ''Remembrance of the Daleks'', depicted Davros being incorporated into the Imperial Casing to sustain his life after he was grievously injured in an explosion, lending weight to the idea that his head was all that was left of his original body. However, {{cs|War of the Daleks (novel)}}, which featured Davros immediately following the events of ''Remembrance of the Daleks'', featured Davros back in his original [[Davros's chair|chair]], complete with his torso and arm.

Accordingly, when Davros returned on television in {{cs|The Stolen Earth (TV story)}}, his organic torso and arm were intact, with his organic body serving as a critical plot point in how he was able to build his [[New Dalek Empire]].

=== Near uses ===
Davros would have appeared in the cancelled [[BBC Eighth Doctor Adventures]] novel {{cs|Enemy of the Daleks (unproduced novel)}}, having degenerated further from a disembodied head in {{cs|Remembrance of the Daleks (TV story)}} into a digitised [[artificial intelligence]].

When concerned about using [[CGI]] in his episodes, [[Russell T Davies]] considered using Davros as a substitute for the [[Dalek Emperor in the Last Great Time War|Emperor Dalek]] in {{cs|The Parting of the Ways (TV story)}} and [[The Beast (The Impossible Planet)|the Beast]] in {{cs|The Satan Pit (TV story)}}.

[[Steven Moffat]] considered having Davros appear in [[The Vault (The Pilot)|the Vault]] during [[Series 10 (Doctor Who)|Series 10]] until he settled on [[Missy]] being the prisoner.

=== Other information ===
* [[Terry Nation]] based Davros' appearance on [[Dan Dare]]'s nemesis [[the Mekon]].
* The ending of {{cs|Genesis of the Daleks (TV story)}} would have shown a button on Davros's wheelchair flashing after his "death", hinting that he had not died, but, due to a production error the detail did not make it into the finished programme.
* [[Michael Wisher]] is credited as "Davros, Supreme Kaled Scientist" on the sleeve of the ''Genesis of the Daleks'' LP.
* Davros was supposed to be killed off for good in {{cs|Resurrection of the Daleks (TV story)}}, until Nation's estate complained.
